entry.title: Clausery v2.119.0 — Added sticky bottom CTA to the remaining invoice-workflow pages (deposit invoice, hourly invoice, final invoice) and the three standalone invoice guides (invoice email template, how to save an invoice as PDF, how to write a payment receipt) which were served out of separate files (site/invoice-email.mjs, invoice-pdf.mjs, payment-receipt.mjs, invoice-workflows.mjs) and therefore missed the earlier blanket CTA rollout. entry.title: Clausery v2.118.0 — Added sticky bottom CTA to the 25 contract-clause explanation pages (/clauses/.html) and the 9 free small-business calculator pages (/free-tools/.html). These are deep-reference pages that readers reach from Google mid-research and often close without converting; the persistent CTA gives them a one-tap "Open Clausery" or "Make an invoice" button after they finish reading. The clause CTA points to the app (contract drafting) and the tool CTA points to the invoice starter (matching invoicing tools like Net-30 due date and late-payment interest calculators). Sticky CTA coverage: 305 → 338 pages. Inline styles only.

entry.title: Clausery v2.115.0 — Switched country, trade and hub/template pages (135 pages total) from og:type=website to og:type=article with proper article:published_time and article:modified_time Open Graph tags and matching Article schema.org JSON-LD. Previously only guides (feed:true) emitted article metadata; now every long-form editorial page announces itself as an article so that social shares, Google News and article-focused rich-result parsers can pick up author/publisher/date signals. The core /templates/ (LIB) pages already did this correctly.

entry.title: Clausery v2.114.0 — Added a persistent primary call-to-action button to all country pages (UK/US/AU/CA/NZ/IE/ZA), every trade template page (contractor, handyman, cleaning, landscaping, photography, videography, graphic design, etc.) and every long-form hub/template/contract page. On mobile the CTA sticks to the bottom of the viewport with safe-area padding so it stays tappable once visitors scroll past the hero; on desktop it floats as a rounded pill in the bottom-right corner. This removes the "scroll back to the top to convert" friction on our longest-tail landing pages, which were already leading in SERPs but losing conversions when readers reached the FAQ without seeing a second CTA. Uses per-page inline styles only — site.css remains capped at 44,959 B.

entry.title: Clausery v2.110.0 — New US invoice template page at /invoice-templates/us-invoice.html — targets the highest-volume head term "free invoice template" (which is overwhelmingly US-intent) with a plain US-dollar, month/day/year invoice for freelancers, contractors and small businesses. Includes guidance on US-specific conventions: Net 30 payment terms, ACH/wire/PayPal/Zelle payment details, late fees (typically 1–1.5%/month if contracted), when sales tax does and does not apply, the lack of a federal invoice format, and EIN/SSN/W-9 privacy. Opens the app pre-set to USD and en-US date formatting. Sitemap grows from 379 to 380 pages.

entry.title: Clausery v2.109.0 — New UK non-VAT invoice template page at /invoice-templates/uk-invoice.html — targets the high-volume "free invoice template UK" search for sole traders, freelancers and small businesses not registered for VAT (turnover under £90k). The page sets the currency to pounds sterling, dates to day/month/year, includes UK-specific guidance on payment terms (Net 30, BACS), the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 interest/compensation wording, and explains when you don't need to show VAT. The existing /invoice-templates/uk-vat-invoice.html page still covers the VAT-registered case. This pairs with updated UK keyword usage on the invoice-templates hub.
